theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Which document records that a new circuit was installed, inspected and tested, and is safe to put into service?
options: A daily site diary entry for that day
A certificate with its schedule of test results
A materials order with the delivery note
The time sheet for every electrician who worked on it

questions.stem: A school asks whether its 25-year-old wiring is still safe to use. Which report answers this?
options: An incident report
A progress report
A commissioning report
A periodic inspection (condition) report

questions.stem: On a condition report, how would an exposed live conductor at a classroom socket be classed?
options: Danger present: needs action at once
Improvement recommended at the next visit
Further investigation at a later date
No action, as the socket still works

questions.stem: A board's circuit chart is missing, but every circuit is safe and correctly protected. How would this usually be classed on a condition report?
options: Danger present
Potentially dangerous
Improvement recommended
Unsatisfactory: disconnect at once

questions.stem: A condition report lists one item classed as 'danger present'. What overall result should the report give?
options: Satisfactory, since most items passed
Satisfactory, with a note added for the client
No overall result until the next inspection
Unsatisfactory, with urgent action recorded

questions.stem: On a schedule of test results, what is recorded against each circuit?
options: The circuit's cost, the supplier and the invoice number
Each test reading, such as continuity, with its unit
The name of the person who first designed the building
The time each test took and the weather on the day

questions.stem: An insulation resistance reading is written in a report as '200'. What is wrong with it?
options: Nothing; the number on its own is clear
It should be written out in words, as 'two hundred'
It has no unit, so 200 Ω and 200 MΩ look alike
It should be rounded down to the nearest 100

questions.stem: An insulation tester shows that a reading is above its top range of 999 MΩ. How should this be recorded?
options: As 'more than 999 MΩ', as shown
As '999 MΩ', dropping the 'more than'
As 'infinite', since it is so high
As 'pass', with no reading at all

questions.stem: Why does a test report record the serial number of each instrument used?
options: To trace results to a calibrated instrument
So the instrument can be insured and sold later
To show the client which brand the firm prefers
To fill the empty space at the foot of the form

questions.stem: During a periodic inspection, the team cannot get into the roof space. What should the report say about it?
options: Nothing, since the roof space was not looked at
That the roof wiring is satisfactory throughout
That all the roof wiring must be treated as dangerous
That it was not inspected, and why, as a limitation

questions.stem: Which is the best description of a fault for a fault report?
options: Lighting circuit 3 was messed up somewhere upstairs
Circuit 3: loose line terminal in the box above Room 12
Something went wrong with the lights in the new block
The lights probably stopped working because of the rain

questions.stem: Which statement in an inspection report is an opinion, and should be marked as one?
options: The RCD tripped at 22 ms on test
Board DB2 has no circuit chart
The cable was probably damaged by rats
The cable sheath is cut 300 mm from the box

questions.stem: In an incident report about a trainee who received a shock at the Centre, in what order should the events be set out?
options: In order of how serious each part was
In the order the witnesses happened to speak
Starting from the conclusion and working back
In the order they happened, with times

questions.stem: A trainee gets a small shock from a faulty extension lead but says he feels fine. What should happen?
options: Report it, record it and have him checked medically
Leave it out of the records since he feels fine
Report it only if he becomes ill in the next week
Mention it to his friends so they keep an eye on him

questions.stem: Which recommendation gives the client clear, usable advice?
options: Fix the electrics in the building soon
The wiring could be better in some places
Replace the cracked socket in Room 4 within 7 days
Get an electrician round to have a look at some point

questions.stem: A hotel's general manager will read your 15-page condition report. What should the first page give her?
options: Every single test reading, set out circuit by circuit
The overall result, the urgent items and costs
A history of the hotel and its owners
A full list of the tools and testers used

questions.stem: Which caption is best for a photo in a fault report?
options: A photo of the big problem we found that morning
Figure 3: scorched terminal, DB1 way 4
A very bad one, see for yourself
Look at this mess! Who did this?

questions.stem: A report shows the earth electrode resistance measured once a month for a year. Which is the best way to show it?
options: A pie chart of the twelve readings
A table of contents for the report
A single photo of the earth rod
A line graph of reading against month

questions.stem: Before you send a test report, a co-worker spots that two circuit numbers have been swapped in the table. What should you do?
options: Send it as it is, since the readings are right
Add a note asking the reader to work it out
Correct it, check the rest, then issue it
Delete those two circuits from the report

questions.stem: Why should test readings be written down at the time of testing, not from memory at the end of the day?
options: Readings are easily forgotten or mixed up
Writing them later makes the sheet look neater
Testers wipe their stored readings after an hour
The client likes to watch each one being written

questions.stem: A circuit failed its first insulation test, was repaired and then passed. What should the report show?
options: Only the passing result after the repair
Neither result, since it now works
Only the first result, as it was the real one
Both results, and the repair made in between

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of a commissioning report for a new pump control panel?
options: To list the price paid for each part inside the panel
To record that it works as designed, with settings
To order the spare parts the client may need
To record the hours each member spent on it

questions.stem: Which content is most useful in a weekly progress report to a site manager?
options: Work done against plan, problems, next week's work
A full copy of the specification and the drawings
Each member's news and how they are feeling
The weather each day and the temperature

questions.stem: Which sentence is clearest for a client who is not an electrician?
options: CPC continuity was outside acceptable parameters
R1+R2 exceeded the maximum value in the tables
The earth wire to the kitchen sockets is not connected
Earthing issue noted; refer to the schedule

questions.stem: Which way of writing an insulation reading follows the usual SI style?
options: 0.5mohm
0.5 Mohms.
0.5 MΩ
0.5 megs

questions.stem: Who should normally decide the scope of a condition report, such as which buildings and circuits it covers?
options: It is agreed with the client before the work
It is left to the newest trainee on the team to choose
It is set by whoever reads the report last
It is set by the firm that sold the cable

questions.stem: Where should the signed installation certificate for a new circuit be kept?
options: In the glovebox of the firm's van
Only as a photo on the electrician's phone
Thrown away once the client has paid
With the client, and a copy in the job file

questions.stem: Why does an installation certificate have separate signatures for the design, the installation, and the inspection and testing?
options: So that the form is long enough to look official
Each person takes responsibility for their part
Because the client must sign it three times
So the inspector can be paid three times

questions.stem: You prepare reports on a tablet on site. What is good practice?
options: Save to the firm's system, which is backed up
Keep them only on the tablet you carry around site
Email them to your own personal account
Print them, then delete the electronic file

questions.stem: A report explains how a neutral shared between two circuits created a shock risk. What would help the reader most?
options: A longer paragraph explaining the theory
A photo of the outside of the building
A simple sketch of the two circuits
The CV of the electrician who found it

questions.stem: Insulation readings for 24 circuits must go in a report. What is the clearest way to present them?
options: As one long sentence in the findings
In a pie chart of the 24 readings
As a list of numbers, without the circuits
In a table with circuit, reading and result

questions.stem: Why should a condition report not be shared outside the client's business without permission?
options: It is far too long for anyone else to read
It holds private details about the property
Other people would find it far too dull to read through
It costs the firm money to send emails

questions.stem: A fault report for a tripping breaker should explain the cause. Which statement gives a cause, not just a symptom?
options: The breaker kept on tripping all afternoon
Water got into an outdoor box past a missing seal
The power went off three times during the day
The client was very unhappy about the trips

questions.stem: Why should an incident report record which PPE was worn and how the circuit was isolated?
options: To show whether the controls worked or failed
To show what the team was wearing that day
To replace the need for witness statements
To let the firm charge the client for the PPE

questions.stem: Why should a near miss, such as a tester showing a 'dead' circuit to be live, be reported?
options: To get the people involved into trouble
Only because the site rules force it
They show a weakness to fix before anyone is hurt
To fill up the empty pages of the site incident book

questions.stem: Which recommendation in a condition report is the most urgent?
options: Repaint the rusty door of the main board
Fit a new label to the outdoor socket
Replace all the old office lights with new LED panel fittings
Cover the exposed live terminals in the pump room

questions.stem: Which detail should appear on every page of a long report, so pages are not lost or mixed up?
options: The writer's home phone number
A short note about the weather
The client's bank details
The report number and 'page 3 of 15'

questions.stem: Why is it better to write a date in a report as '4 March 2026' rather than '4/3/26'?
options: It makes the report look longer
Computers cannot read dates in numbers
Readers may take 4/3 as March or as April
It is cheaper to print in words

questions.stem: You are asked to report on a fault in work that your own team did. What should the report do?
options: State the facts, including your team's part
Leave out anything about your own team
Blame the supplier of the materials instead
Wait until everyone has forgotten the fault

questions.stem: A report must compare a school's electricity use in the month before and the month after LED lights were fitted. Which is best?
options: A pie chart of the whole year's use
A bar chart of the before and after months
A photo of the meter on the last day
A list of every lamp that was changed, room by room

questions.stem: Before you sign a schedule of test results, what should you check?
options: That the handwriting is neat and tidy
That it is filled in with a blue pen
That every circuit has all its readings
That the client has already paid the bill

questions.stem: When you hand a client a report on new work, what should you explain to them in person?
options: The main findings and any action they must take
Where you are going on your next holiday
What the firm is doing for its other clients
Nothing, since a good report should speak for itself

questions.stem: Where it is safe, why should an incident report include a photo or sketch of the scene before anything is moved?
options: To make the report look more attractive
To show the client how busy the team has been all week
Only because insurers always like photos
It shows the conditions exactly as they were

questions.stem: Which is the best way to check that your report's recommendations will be understood?
options: Read it through once more by yourself
Ask someone like the reader what they would do
Add more pages so nothing is missed
Use more technical words to sound expert

questions.stem: A client asks only whether her new outdoor light circuit is safe. Which kind of report suits?
options: A 30-page report on the whole house
A phone call, with nothing in writing
A short certificate with the test results
A text message saying 'all good'

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What name is given to a report that records the condition of an existing installation and lists its defects?
On a condition report, which word is used for an item that is not dangerous now but would make the installation safer if fixed? (It begins with 'i'.)
What do we call an event in which nobody was hurt, but someone could have been?
What is the name of the table that lists each circuit's test readings?
A circuit's insulation resistance was 2 MΩ before repair and 200 MΩ after. How many times larger is the reading after the repair?
What word names an event at work in which someone was hurt or property was damaged, and which must be reported on a set form?
What is the name of the certificate given for a small addition to one existing circuit, such as an extra socket?
What word is used for the section of a condition report that lists parts that could not be inspected, and why?
A schedule shows 30 circuits, of which 27 passed all their tests. What percentage passed?
What is the name for the date by which a test instrument must next be checked against a known standard?
What is the name of the book or record in which a site team writes each day's work, visitors and instructions?
In a report, what word comes before the number of a drawing, chart or photo, as in '___ 2'?
What one word describes the overall result of a condition report when one or more items are classed as dangerous?
What word names the part of a report that tells the client what should be done next?
A report recommends the next inspection in 5 years. How many months is that?

essays.stem: Your team is asked to carry out a periodic inspection of a small school block in St Ann's Bay and write a condition report. Describe how you would plan the work, and the main sections the report should contain.
essays.modelAnswer: First I agree the scope with the school: which buildings and circuits, when the power can be off, and any areas we cannot reach. I collect the old drawings and certificates. On the day, the team inspects visually first: accessories, cables, boards, earthing and bonding. Then, with circuits safely isolated, locked off and proved dead with a tester checked before and after, we carry out the dead tests, and an authorised person does any live tests such as RCD tests. Readings are written on the schedule at the time. The report should have: the client's details and the address; the purpose and the agreed scope; the limitations, such as a locked roof space; a summary of the general condition; a list of observations, each with its location and a class (danger present, potentially dangerous, improvement recommended); the overall result (satisfactory or unsatisfactory); recommendations with time limits and the next inspection date; and the schedule of test results, with instrument details. It is signed and dated.
markingPoints: Agrees scope, timing and access with the client and gathers old records
Inspects visually, then tests with safe isolation and records readings at the time
Report includes client details, purpose, scope and limitations
Observations listed with location and a danger class, and an overall result
Recommendations with time limits, next inspection date, test schedule, signature and date

essays.stem: A bakery in May Pen calls your firm because a breaker trips several times a week. After the fault is found and fixed, you must write a fault report. Explain what the report should include, and why.
essays.modelAnswer: The report starts with the client's name, the address, the date, and who carried out the work. It states the complaint in the client's words: the breaker for the oven circuit trips several times a week, usually in the morning. Then it gives what we did: the checks and tests, with the readings and units, and the instruments used. It states the cause, not just the symptom, for example: 'The insulation between line and earth in the outdoor junction box was low because rain water was entering through a missing gland seal.' It describes the repair: a new gland and box fitted, and the retest readings showing the circuit now passes. It includes a labelled photo of the fault before repair. Finally, it gives recommendations, such as checking the other outdoor boxes, and the date for follow-up. This lets the client see what was wrong and that it is fixed, and gives the firm a record if the fault returns.
markingPoints: Client details, date and who did the work
The complaint described clearly
Tests and readings with units and instruments
Cause and repair stated, with retest results and a photo
Recommendations and follow-up; explains why the record matters

essays.stem: A trainee received a shock, without injury, while working on a training board that a classmate said was isolated. Describe how you would investigate this and write the incident report.
essays.modelAnswer: First, the board is made safe and the trainee is checked by a first-aider and sent for a medical check, because a shock can affect the heart later. The area is left as it was where safe, and photos are taken. I talk to the trainee and the classmate separately, and to any witnesses, and write down what each says. I check the isolation: which switch was off, whether a lock and tag were used, and whether the board was proved dead with a tester checked before and after. The report gives the date, time and place, the people involved, and a step-by-step account of what happened, in time order. It states the facts found, for example: 'The wrong breaker was switched off; no lock was fitted; the board was not proved dead.' It gives the root cause and the actions agreed, such as retraining on safe isolation and checking locks at every board. The report is signed, dated and sent to the instructor and the Centre's safety officer.
markingPoints: Makes safe and gets first aid and a medical check
Preserves the scene, takes photos and gets statements separately
Checks what isolation steps were or were not followed
Report gives time-ordered facts, root cause and actions
Signed, dated and sent to the right people

essays.stem: Explain how defects found during a periodic inspection are classed by danger, giving an example for each class, and say how the classes affect the overall result and the urgency of repairs.
essays.modelAnswer: Defects are usually put in three classes. 'Danger present' means there is a risk of injury now, for example a broken socket with live parts exposed. It must be made safe at once, and the client is told immediately, in writing. 'Potentially dangerous' means it could become dangerous if another fault happens, for example a metal light fitting with no earth connection. It needs urgent repair. 'Improvement recommended' means it is not dangerous but would make the installation safer or better, for example a missing circuit chart. Where something cannot be checked, the report may say that further investigation is needed. If any item is classed as danger present or potentially dangerous, the overall result is unsatisfactory, even if everything else is good. If there are only improvement items, the result can be satisfactory. The class tells the client how quickly to act, so the report should state a time limit for each item.
markingPoints: Danger present explained with a correct example and immediate action
Potentially dangerous explained with a correct example and urgent action
Improvement recommended explained with a correct example
Any danger or potentially dangerous item makes the result unsatisfactory
Classes tell the client how urgent each repair is

essays.stem: Explain how to record dead test results accurately on a schedule of test results, and what to do when a reading is out of range or a circuit fails.
essays.modelAnswer: Before testing, I fill in the circuit details from the board: circuit number, what it feeds, the protective device, and the cable size. I record the instrument used, with its serial number and calibration date. As each test is done, I write the reading straight onto the schedule against the right circuit, with its unit, for example 0.45 Ω for continuity or more than 200 MΩ for insulation, exactly as the instrument shows. I do not round or guess. If a test cannot be done, I write 'not tested' and the reason, rather than leaving a blank. I compare each reading with the limit in the specification or the tables. If a reading fails, I mark it clearly, the circuit is not energised, and the fault is found and repaired. I then retest and record the new reading, keeping the failed reading and a note of the repair. Finally, I check every line is complete, sign and date the schedule.
markingPoints: Fills in circuit details and instrument serial number and calibration
Records each reading at once, against the right circuit, with units, exactly as shown
Writes 'not tested' with a reason instead of leaving blanks
Compares with limits; a failed circuit is not energised
Repairs, retests, records both results, then checks, signs and dates

essays.stem: Describe what should be included in a commissioning report for a new pump control panel at a housing scheme, and why each part matters.
essays.modelAnswer: The report gives the client, the site, the panel's reference and the date, so it can be traced. It lists the equipment installed with makers' details and serial numbers, which helps with warranty claims and spares. It records the dead test results, such as continuity and insulation resistance, with the instruments used, showing it was safe to switch on. It records the settings made, such as the overload setting from the motor's full-load current and the timer and level-switch settings, so anyone servicing it later knows how it was set. It records the function tests done by an authorised person: the pump starts and stops at the right levels, it turns the right way, and the alarms and overload trip work. It lists any items still to be done, with dates. It notes that the manuals and drawings were handed over and the client's staff were shown how to operate it. Finally, it is signed by the person who commissioned it and by the client.
markingPoints: Identification: client, site, panel reference, date
Equipment list with serial numbers
Dead test results and instruments
Settings and function tests recorded by an authorised person
Outstanding items, handover of manuals and training, signatures

essays.stem: A school in Old Harbour replaced its fluorescent lights with LED fittings. Explain how you would use tables, a graph and photos in a short report showing the effect on its electricity use.
essays.modelAnswer: I would collect the monthly kWh readings from the school's bills or meter for six months before and six months after the change. I would put them in a table with the month, the kWh used and the cost in J$, with units in the column headings and a total at the bottom, so the reader can check the figures. Then I would draw a bar chart with the months along the bottom axis and kWh up the side, with the 'before' and 'after' bars in different shades and a key, so the drop can be seen at a glance. The chart has a title and labelled axes with units. I would add numbered photos with captions, such as 'Figure 2: new LED panel in Classroom 4', to show what was installed. In the text, I refer to each table and figure by number and explain what it shows, for example: 'Table 1 shows use fell by about 30%.' I would note anything else that may have changed, such as school holidays.
markingPoints: Collects real before-and-after data with units
Clear table with headings, units and totals
Suitable chart with title, labelled axes, units and key
Numbered photos with clear captions
Refers to each figure in the text and notes other factors

essays.stem: Your team is rewiring a guest house in Port Antonio over three weeks, and is now four days behind because the light fittings arrived late. Describe what your weekly progress report to the manager should contain.
essays.modelAnswer: The report gives the job name, the week number, the date and who wrote it. It states the work completed this week against the plan, for example: 'Ground floor conduit and cables complete; first floor 60% complete.' It states clearly that the job is four days behind, and gives the cause: the light fittings arrived four days late, so the team could not fit and test the lighting circuits as planned. It explains what the team did meanwhile, such as moving ahead with socket circuits. It gives the effect on the finish date, and the options to recover, for example working an extra Saturday or adding a member, with their cost. It asks the manager for any decisions needed. It lists the work planned for next week, any safety issues or near misses, and any changes asked for by the client. It is short, factual and sent on time, so the manager can act early.
markingPoints: Identification: job, week, date, writer
Progress against the plan
States the delay, its cause and what the team did meanwhile
Gives the effect on the finish date and recovery options for decision
Next week's work, safety issues and client changes; short and on time

essays.stem: Explain how the reports and certificates for a finished installation should be handed over to a client, and which records the firm should keep, and why.
essays.modelAnswer: At handover I give the client the signed installation certificate with its schedule of test results, the as-built drawings, the circuit chart in the board, and the makers' manuals and warranties. I go through the main points in person: the overall result, any items still outstanding and when they will be done, how to switch off in an emergency, how and when to press the RCD test buttons, and when the next inspection is due. I ask the client to sign to say they received the documents. The firm keeps copies of the certificates, test results, drawings, the handover receipt and any reports of faults or incidents in the job file, in paper or in a backed-up computer system. These are kept for as long as the firm's rules and any law require, often many years. They show the work was done and tested properly if there is a later fault, claim or inspection, and help anyone who works on the installation later.
markingPoints: Hands over certificate, test results, as-built drawings, chart, manuals
Explains results, outstanding items, emergency switching, RCD testing, next inspection
Gets a signed receipt from the client
Firm keeps copies securely in a job file or backed-up system for the required time
Explains why: evidence for faults, claims, inspections and future work

essays.stem: A client's new air-conditioning circuit keeps tripping. You must write a short report comparing two solutions: fitting a larger cable and breaker, or running a new circuit from a new sub-board. Explain how you would set out the report and present the two options.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start with a title, the client, the date and my name, then a short summary giving the problem and my recommendation, so a busy reader sees it first. The introduction explains the problem and what I was asked to do. The findings give the facts: the unit's current from its rating plate, the existing cable and breaker sizes, the length of the run, and the test results. Then I describe each option in turn under the same headings: what work is needed, how it solves the problem, the cost in J$ (with GCT at the current rate), the time and power shut-down needed, and any risks. A simple table comparing the two options side by side helps the client decide. The conclusion says which option best meets the client's needs and why, based on the facts. I end with clear recommendations and the next steps. Calculations and readings go in an appendix.
markingPoints: Title details and a short summary with the recommendation first
Introduction and factual findings (load, existing sizes, length, tests)
Each option described under the same headings, including cost and time
Comparison table to help the client decide
Conclusion based on facts, clear recommendation and appendix for workings

practical1.title: Inspect and dead-test a training installation, and write a condition report with a schedule of test results
practical1.brief: The assessor has set up a training installation with a distribution board and several circuits, with some defects (for example a missing circuit chart, a cracked accessory, a missing earth connection and a low insulation reading). As a group, agree the scope and share the circuits so every member inspects and tests at least one. The board is isolated, locked and tagged by every member, and proved dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after; it stays dead throughout. Each member inspects their circuits, carries out continuity, insulation resistance and polarity tests, records each reading at once on the schedule of test results with its unit, and photographs any defect with a caption. Together, the group writes a condition report: details, scope and limitations, observations each with a location and a danger class, an overall result, recommendations with time limits, and the schedule attached. One member checks the whole report against the readings before it is signed. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Training installation with a distribution board, lockable isolator and set defects
Padlocks, danger tags, multi-lock hasp, voltage tester and proving unit
Continuity and insulation resistance tester (or multifunction tester on its dead tests), with its serial number and calibration date
Blank schedule of test results and condition report forms
Phone or camera, labels and a rule for photos
photos: The isolated board with every member's lock and tag
The tester on the proving unit before and after proving dead
Each member recording a reading on the schedule
Each defect, with a rule or label and its caption
The completed schedule of test results
The finished condition report, signed after checking
checklist: Took part in safe isolation and kept the installation dead
Inspected their circuits and found the defects present
Carried out the dead tests correctly and recorded each reading at once, with its unit
Gave each defect a clear location and a sensible danger class
Wrote clear, specific recommendations with time limits
Took part in checking the report against the readings
Used plain, factual language with no guesses presented as fact
safety: The installation stays isolated, locked and tagged throughout; prove dead with a tester checked before and after
Warn others before an insulation test, keep hands off the conductors, and let the circuit discharge after
Do not remove any cover the assessor has not approved; the assessor removes covers where needed

practical2.title: Investigate a repeated tripping fault on a dead training board and write a fault report with a chart
practical2.brief: The assessor gives the group a 'client complaint' and a two-week trip log from a small shop (date, time, which breaker tripped and what was in use), and a training board that copies the shop's circuits with a set fault. As a group, first analyse the trip log: each member takes part in tallying the trips by circuit and by time of day, and the group draws a bar chart by hand or on a computer. Then, with the board isolated, locked and tagged and proved dead with a tester checked before and after, members take turns to carry out dead tests to find the fault, recording readings with units and photographing the fault with a caption. Together the group writes a fault report: details, the complaint, the analysis with the table and chart, tests and readings, the cause, the repair and retest, and recommendations. Each member writes at least one section, and another member checks it. One member hands the report over to the assessor as if to the client, explaining the main points. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Client complaint and two-week trip log from the assessor
Training board with a set fault, lockable isolator, padlocks and tags
Graph paper or a computer with a spreadsheet
Fault report form or template, rulers, labels and a phone or camera
photos: The tally table made from the trip log
The finished bar chart with title, labelled axes and units
The isolated board and the tester on the proving unit
A member taking a test reading
The fault found, with a caption
The finished fault report and the handover to the assessor
checklist: Took part in tallying the trip log correctly
Helped draw a chart with a title, labelled axes, units and key where needed
Followed safe isolation and kept the board dead while testing
Recorded test readings accurately with units
Wrote at least one clear, factual section of the report
Checked another member's section and corrected errors
Report states the cause, not just the symptom, and gives clear recommendations
safety: The board stays isolated, locked and tagged during testing; prove dead with a tester checked before and after
Warn others before an insulation test and keep hands off the conductors during it
Only the assessor energises the board after the repair is checked
